title: Access intake priority lattice and SLA gating for identity & admin requests
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and Sales/Support are submitting a growing volume of non-bug access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). Current intake is ad-hoc (email/Slack/handoffs), causing long SLAs, inconsistent prioritization, security review delays, and engineering context-switching.

Goal: Define a repeatable intake & triage system for admin/access requests that: (1) assigns deterministic priority with a weighted matrix (security/regulatory sensitivity, revenue/ARR impact, number of users affected, automation/engineering effort), (2) enforces SLA gating for high-risk work, (3) automates routing to Support/Account/Eng queues, and (4) provides a lightweight runbook for security and PM review. This ticket scopes the PM work to design the matrix, prototype intake form, establish routing rules, and own rollout documentation and training. Engineering delivery (routing automation, dashboarding) will be tracked as dependent ENG tickets.
scope: Design priority lattice + gating rules, intake form fields and label mappings, routing policies (support queue, enterprise ops, eng), acceptance criteria and success metrics, draft runbook for security sign-off, training checklist for AE/Support. Prototype in Zendesk/Intercom or internal Intake form and Linear label mapping.
out_of_scope: Full automation of SCIM provisioning logic, RBAC enforcement plumbing in product, one-off engineering work to implement custom customer integrations (those will be triaged to engineering stories). Detailed SSO metadata validation scripts — security will own final signing policy.
success_metrics: Median triage-to-assignment time for enterprise access requests reduced from 5 days to <48 hours
% of high-risk requests with security approval timestamped within SLA: 90%
Queue backlog (open access requests) reduced by 50% within two cycles
Customer satisfaction (NPS for onboarding tickets) for enterprise identity work improves by +10 points
acceptance_criteria: Priority lattice documented in Confluence with scoring weights and examples for RBAC, SSO, SCIM, org policy exception requests

Prototype intake form created with required fields (customer tier, users affected, regulatory/regulatory flags, requested change, requested-by, estimated eng effort), and mapping to Linear labels and priority score
Routing rules defined and implemented in Support workflow (Zendesk macros/Intercom rules or internal intake) that tag and route to enterprise-ops or eng on threshold
SLA gating policy documented (e.g., high-risk requests require security ack within 48h; engineering SLO for dedicated capacity requests defined)
Runbook draft reviewed & approved by Security and Head of Support
Dashboard proto (Looker/Grafana) with queue latency, time-to-security-approval, and per-customer SLA breach counts is available to stakeholders
implementation_steps: Research: compile 25 recent access requests and classify by outcome, time-to-resolve, and customer tier (owner: Liam)
Draft weighted-priority lattice with scoring rubric and worked examples (owner: Ava)
Prototype intake form in Zendesk + map to Linear labels + automation rules (owner: Support Ops)
Create Linear templates and label-to-queue mapping; add new PM/Eng triage label set (owner: Solutions Eng)
Security review of gating definitions; incorporate feedback into runbook (owner: Security)
Build dashboard queries for queue metrics and SLA breaches (owner: Data)
Pilot with two strategic customers for 3 weeks and iterate on weights and fields (owner: AE + PM)
Rollout internal training sessions for AE/Support and publish playbook in Confluence (owner: PM)
Handoff dependent engineering work with clear ACs and discovery notes (create ENG stories)
risks: Overweighting revenue could deprioritize high-security but low-revenue customers — mitigated by a ’security override’ flag
Support tooling limits (Zendesk rule expressiveness) may require engineering automation work — tracked as ENG dependency
Customers with bespoke identity setups will still need manual engineering time — ensure expectation-setting in runbook
Ambiguous intake fields will lead to rework; minimize by providing examples and required attachments
